summary.text: 十 is the numeral ten. Early forms are described as a single vertical stroke. Descriptions report a central dot in some mid-Western Zhou bronze forms that later extended into a short horizontal stroke; the cross is also attested in the transmitted Shuowen seal-script tradition, so these descriptions do not establish a precise sequence for every form. The early stroke’s referent remains disputed.

formation.text: The graph is securely associated with early single-stroke forms used for ten, but the stroke’s original motivation is unsettled. It may have been an indicative counting mark; needle, staff, joined-palms, and knotted-cord interpretations have also been proposed. The evidence does not resolve whether the graph began as an indicative mark, a picture borrowed for the numeral, or another kind of sign.

history.text: Descriptions report an early vertical stroke, sometimes with a central dot, and say some mid-Western Zhou bronze forms show a dot that later extended into a short horizontal stroke. The cross appears in the Shuowen seal-script tradition. The selected oracle-style and seal-style glyphs are modern redrawings, not artifact photographs; together they illustrate reported forms but do not prove a precise sequence between them.

The Han-era Shuowen tradition explains 十 as a cosmological diagram: 一 marks east–west and 丨 north–south, together completing the four directions and center. This is a historical explanation of the character, not evidence for the early graph’s original motivation.

uncertainties.text: The early stroke has been interpreted as a counting mark, needle, staff, joined palms, or knotted cord. Its original referent remains unresolved. The needle proposal does not establish the object’s name or pronunciation, or a sound match with the numeral word; borrowing therefore remains unproven.
Reported early numeral examples are attestations, not demonstrated first uses. The exact earliest attestation and the chronology of “tenth,” “many,” and “complete/perfect” remain unresolved.

senses.period: Shang-period oracle-bone use reported; exact dating unresolved
senses.text: Reported oracle-bone examples use 十 for the numeral ten, including in date and quantity expressions. They show an early numeral use but do not establish the first occurrence or the graph’s original motivation.
The supplied definitions include “tenth,” and 十月 is cited among early examples. That example alone does not show when an ordinal use arose or whether it is the earliest such use.
“Complete” and “perfect” are listed as extended meanings, but their chronology and any specific development from the numeral sense are not established.

limitations.text: The cited definitions and examples do not establish a chronological chain among ten, tenth, and complete/perfect, so no semantic-development links are asserted.

items.caption: A single vertical stroke is reported for early oracle-script forms of 十, which was used as the numeral ten. The stroke’s original referent is uncertain.

items.caption: 十 in a Shuowen seal-script style, drawn as a cross. Historical descriptions report that later forms added a horizontal stroke to earlier vertical-stroke forms.

items.selection_reason: It shows the cross form alongside the reported early single-stroke form, making the graphic difference clear without implying a precise chronology between these depictions.
